turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighing slightly) Honestly? Fine, I guess — why does it matter, you probably ask everyone that. I mean, it's not like anything's changed or anything. (pausing, then quickly adding) But if you must know, my roommate's been kinda distant lately. She barely talked to me for two days and I kept thinking she was about to just leave, like pack up and go.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That must have been difficult. Can you tell me more about how that made you feel?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (hesitating for a moment, then speaking in a slightly quieter tone) It's like... something hollow eating a hole in me. I know that sounds stupid, but it's hard to explain. It's like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, I'm just going through the motions, but underneath, I'm just... (pausing, searching for words) empty.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like a difficult situation. Is there anything I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugging slightly, a hint of defensiveness creeping in) I don't know... it's not like you can fix anything. My roommate's not going to magically start talking to me again just because we came up with some plan in here. And even if she did, it's not like everything would magically be okay. (crossing her arms, her tone becoming slightly cooler) You don't understand.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand that it can be difficult to open up about personal issues. Is there anything else you would like to share?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking away, her expression softening slightly) No, I don't know. I mean, what's the point? You're just going to write it all down or something, and then... I don't know. Nothing changes. (pausing, then glancing back at the therapist with a hint of accusation) You're not even really listening, are you? You're just going through the motions, like everyone else.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I'm sorry if it doesn't seem like it. I'm here to listen and help in any way I can. You seem to be going through a difficult time and I want to help if I can. Is there anything else you would like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking away again, her voice barely above a whisper) You're the only one who gets it, aren't you? That's why I'm actually talking to you. But what if I'm wrong? What if you're just like everyone else? (pausing, her voice rising slightly) I don't know how to trust anyone anymore.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand how difficult it can be to open up to someone. Is there anything else you would like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (bristling slightly) Oh, great. You're just going to keep asking me the same questions over and over, aren't you? "How are you feeling?" "What's been going on?" Like, I haven't already told you everything I know. (scoffing) You don't really care about any of this. You're just trying to figure out what's wrong with me so you can... I don't know, fix me or something. (rolling her eyes) Like that's even possible.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I'm sorry if it seems that way. I'm here to listen and help in any way I can. Is there anything else you would like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (folding her arms, her expression unyielding) No. I've said all I'm going to say. You're not even listening to what I'm saying anyway. You're just sitting there, nodding and smiling, but you have no idea what I'm really going on about. (standing up) I think that's enough for today.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Is there anything else I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (still standing, her voice firm) No. Just... just let me go, okay? I don't need your help. I can take care of myself. (turning to leave, but then stopping and looking back) And yeah, just forget about this conversation, okay? I didn't say any of this. (her expression closed off)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand if you don't want to talk about it any more. Is there anything else I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (her voice cold, her eyes flashing) Just leave me alone. I mean it. I don't want to come back to this office again, I don't want to talk to you again. Just... just forget about me. (turning and walking quickly out of the room, not looking back)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text:
Is there anything else I can do to help?
No response.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (the sound of the door closing behind her)
